summary.text: Tommy Tuberville is Alabama's senior U.S. senator and a former college football head coach, including at Auburn University from 1999 to 2008.

First elected to the Senate in 2020, he won the November 3, 2026 election for governor as the Republican nominee, defeating Democrat Doug Jones, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.

paragraphs.text: Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, and earned a B.S. in physical education from Southern State College (now Southern Arkansas University) in 1976.

He began coaching high school football in 1976 and was head football coach at Ole Miss from 1995 to 1998, Auburn from 1999 to 2008, Texas Tech from 2010 to 2012 and Cincinnati from 2013 to 2016, and he worked as a broadcaster for ESPN in 2017.

In 2020, in his first political campaign, Tuberville was elected to the U.S. Senate, defeating incumbent Democrat Doug Jones. He announced in 2025 that he would run for governor, and he and Jones won their parties' nominations in May 2026.
His campaign ran on an "Alabama First Agenda" of cutting taxes and government waste, expanding school choice, protecting Second Amendment rights and tougher border enforcement.
Tommy Tuberville won the November 3, 2026 general election for governor with 52% of the vote to Doug Jones's 48%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
